descriptors.concept_name: Objective and Scope of Ind AS 19
descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes accounting and disclosure for employee benefits, requiring entities to recognize a liability for services received and an expense when economic benefits are consumed. Accrual accounting principles govern these obligations so that employment costs are recorded in the periods corresponding to the services rendered.
exclusion: Share-based payment transactions under Ind AS 102
Reporting by employee benefit plans themselves
nearby_distinctions: Unlike equity transactions with owners, employee benefits are operating expenses reflecting consumption of services.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 19 applies to all employer accounting for employee benefits except those covered under share-based payment standards. The framework encompasses formal agreements, legal mandates, and informal practices that generate constructive obligations.
inclusion: Nation, state, or industry multi-employer contributions
exclusion: Financial reporting by employee benefit plans
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general liability recognition by specifically addressing obligations arising from human resource deployment and service contracts.

descriptors.definition: Employee benefits include all forms of consideration given by an entity in exchange for services rendered or for the termination of employment. These provisions extend to payments made directly to employees, their dependents, beneficiaries, or external third parties such as insurance companies.
inclusion: Permanent, casual, and temporary worker benefits
exclusion: Equity instruments governed strictly under share-based payment standards
nearby_distinctions: Encompasses direct remuneration as well as indirect provisions channeled to family members or insurance providers.

descriptors.definition: Employee benefits are categorized into short-term, post-employment, other long-term, and termination benefits based on their timing and settlement characteristics. Each classification requires distinct measurement rules reflecting when the related service is performed and when the liability is expected to be extinguished.
inclusion: Wages, salaries, and social security contributions
exclusion: Transactions addressed by other non-employment accounting standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by the expected period of settlement relative to the annual reporting date rather than the nature of the work.

descriptors.definition: Short-term benefits are expected to be settled wholly before twelve months after the annual reporting period, whereas post-employment and other long-term benefits are payable after completion of employment or over extended periods. Termination benefits specifically arise from the early cessation of an employment contract.
inclusion: Annual salaries and paid sick leave
nearby_distinctions: Separates short-term settlement timelines from post-employment obligations requiring actuarial discounting.

descriptors.concept_name: Definitions Relating To Classification Of Plans
descriptors.definition: Post-employment benefit plans comprise formal or informal arrangements to provide benefits upon completion of employment, categorized into defined contribution and defined benefit plans. Multi-employer plans pool assets from unrelated entities to provide common benefits without linking contributions to a specific employer's staff profile.
nearby_distinctions: Defined contribution plans cap the entity's risk via fixed payments, whereas defined benefit plans expose the entity to actuarial and investment risks.

descriptors.concept_name: Definitions Relating To The Net Defined Benefit Liability (Asset)
descriptors.definition: Net defined benefit liability or asset is the plan deficit or surplus adjusted for any asset ceiling limits. Plan assets and qualifying insurance policies are measured at fair value to offset the present value of the defined benefit obligation.
terminology: Present Value of Defined Benefit Obligation
inclusion: Funds held in legally separate long-term employee benefit entities
Insurance policies issued by unrelated parties dedicated to funding benefits
exclusion: Non-transferable financial instruments issued by the reporting entity itself
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general corporate assets and restricted plan assets unavailable to general creditors.

descriptors.concept_name: Definitions Relating To Defined Benefit Cost
descriptors.definition: Defined benefit cost comprises service cost, net interest on the net defined benefit liability or asset, and remeasurements. Service cost includes current service cost, past service cost from plan amendments, and gains or losses on settlements.
inclusion: Impact of plan amendments and curtailments
Actuarial experience adjustments and assumption changes
exclusion: Standard administrative costs of managing general corporate operations
nearby_distinctions: Isolates the time-value interest component and actuarial volatility from standard operational service expenses.

descriptors.definition: Short-term employee benefits are undiscounted obligations expected to be settled wholly within twelve months after the end of the annual reporting period. They encompass wages, salaries, paid absences, profit-sharing, and non-monetary perks provided to current workers.
exclusion: Post-employment retirement benefits requiring actuarial valuation
nearby_distinctions: Measured without actuarial discounting because settlement occurs within a short twelve-month horizon.

descriptors.concept_name: Recognition And Measurement Of Short-Term Benefits
descriptors.definition: Short-term benefits are recognized as an undiscounted liability after deducting any amounts already paid, or as a prepaid expense if excess payments generate future economic reductions. Paid absences are categorized into accumulating and non-accumulating types based on whether unused entitlements carry forward.
inclusion: Vesting and non-vesting accumulating leave entitlements
exclusion: Long-term sabbatical leaves evaluated under separate multi-period models
nearby_distinctions: Requires immediate expense recognition for non-accumulating absences only when the absence actually occurs.

descriptors.definition: Short-term paid absences allow employees to take time off for holidays, illness, or family milestones while continuing to receive compensation. Accumulating forms carry forward to future periods and may be vesting, granting cash payouts upon exit, or non-vesting.
inclusion: Sick leave and maternity leave compensations
nearby_distinctions: Vesting leave provisions create immediate exit-settlement obligations, whereas non-vesting entitlements depend on continued service utilization.

descriptors.definition: Profit-sharing and bonus obligations are recognized when an entity has a present legal or constructive obligation resulting from past events and a reliable estimate can be made. Because these payments stem from employee service, they are recorded as operating expenses rather than equity distributions.
inclusion: Informal bonus practices generating constructive obligations
nearby_distinctions: Classified as operating expenses rather than profit distributions because the obligation arises directly from employee labor input.
